speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing episodes of unresponsiveness with facial grimacing; to begin our evaluation, have you noticed any specific triggers, such as flashing lights, strong emotions, or lack of sleep, right before these episodes occur? Additionally, how long does each episode typically last?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Absence Epilepsy with Automatisms (likely complex focal seizures evolving into absence or atypical absence), given the 7-year-old age, post-ictal confusion/lethargy, and oral automatisms (grimacing, hand gestures), though the "muddy taste" (gustatory aura) and 3–4 minute duration suggest a focal seizure with secondary generalization rather than typical absence; I recommend requesting EEG to confirm.
